conditions.name: Acute otitis media

triage.label: See a doctor soon
triage.action: Book an appointment in the next few days

conditions.summary: Infection behind the eardrum, usually in a child after a cold. Deep ear pain, fever and muffled hearing, often relieved suddenly if the drum perforates.
workup: Otoscopy for a bulging red drum
Review if no better in 3 days

exam.positive: Tragal or pinna traction pain is characteristic
A swollen, debris-filled canal
Raises the risk of necrotising otitis externa

conditions.name: Otitis externa

triage.label: See a doctor soon
triage.action: Book an appointment in the next few days

conditions.summary: Infection of the ear canal itself. The ear is exquisitely tender when the lobe is tugged, often after swimming or cotton bud use, and the canal weeps.

exam.positive: Abnormal head impulse with unidirectional nystagmus supports a peripheral cause
Able to walk, though veering, unlike cerebellar stroke
Preserved hearing distinguishes from labyrinthitis

labs.test: HINTS is more sensitive than early MRI for stroke

conditions.name: Vestibular neuritis

triage.label: See a doctor soon
triage.action: Book an appointment in the next few days

conditions.summary: Inflammation of the balance nerve after a viral illness. Constant severe spinning for days on end, not triggered by position, with vomiting and unsteadiness.

exam.positive: Sensorineural pattern on the affected side
Normal, excluding other causes
Horizontal nystagmus

conditions.name: Meniere's disease

triage.label: See a doctor soon
triage.action: Book an appointment in the next few days

conditions.summary: Recurrent attacks of vertigo lasting 20 minutes to several hours, each with fluctuating hearing loss, ringing and a feeling of fullness in the same ear.

exam.step: Ask the patient to raise their eyebrows
exam.positive: Forehead involvement confirms a lower motor neurone lesion
Incomplete closure risks exposure keratopathy
Vesicles indicate Ramsay Hunt syndrome

labs.confirms: Forehead sparing means urgent stroke assessment

labs.test: Serology only if atypical or bilateral

conditions.name: Bell's palsy

triage.label: See a doctor soon
triage.action: Book an appointment in the next few days

conditions.summary: Sudden weakness of one whole side of the face, forehead included, from facial nerve inflammation. If the forehead still wrinkles, think stroke instead.
workup: Urgent review if any limb signs

exam.positive: The pinna is pushed forward and outward
Tenderness, swelling and fluctuance
Usually an abnormal drum with discharge

labs.confirms: Post-auricular swelling with a protruding pinna confirms at the bedside

conditions.name: Mastoiditis

triage.label: Emergency
triage.action: Call emergency services or go to an emergency department now

conditions.summary: Infection spreading from the middle ear into the mastoid bone behind it. The ear is pushed forward by a red, boggy, tender swelling. Needs admission.

exam.step: Ask whether hearing loss came on gradually over time, or suddenly
exam.positive: A gradual reduction is typical of wax; sudden hearing loss is NOT typical and needs separate, prompt assessment

exam.step: Ask about ear pain, discharge, or vertigo
exam.positive: None of these are typical of simple wax impaction -- their presence should prompt a different assessment, not reassurance

exam.step: Otoscopy to directly visualise the ear canal
exam.positive: Confirms wax occluding the view of the eardrum -- the definitive bedside finding

labs.confirms: Directly visualises occluding wax against the eardrum -- confirms the diagnosis at the bedside

conditions.name: Ear wax impaction

triage.label: Self-care
triage.action: This can usually be managed at home

conditions.summary: Gradual reduction in hearing, a sensation of blockage or fullness in the ear, sometimes mild discomfort or ringing -- very common and entirely benign. One of the most common, entirely benign causes of reduced hearing in any clinic, easily missed when a checker only routes reduced hearing to serious causes like Meniere's disease or otitis media. Sudden hearing loss, pain, discharge or vertigo are NOT typical of simple wax impaction and need separate assessment.
workup: Ear drops (olive oil or sodium bicarbonate) to soften the wax
Irrigation or microsuction if not cleared by drops alone
Avoid cotton buds, which often push wax further in

redFlags.label: Possible sepsis
redFlags.message: A fever together with confusion, very fast breathing, mottled skin or a collapsing blood pressure can mean infection is affecting the whole body.
redFlags.action: Call emergency services now. Do not wait to see whether it settles.

redFlags.label: Rash that does not fade under pressure
redFlags.message: Spots that stay visible when a glass is pressed on them, alongside feeling unwell, can be a sign of bacteria in the bloodstream.

redFlags.label: Possible severe allergic reaction
redFlags.message: Swelling of the throat or tongue with difficulty breathing after a food, sting, or medicine can close the airway within minutes.
redFlags.action: Use an adrenaline auto-injector if you have one, then call emergency services.

redFlags.label: Reduced consciousness
redFlags.message: Being difficult to rouse, or drifting in and out of awareness, always needs immediate assessment whatever the cause.
redFlags.action: Call emergency services now. Place the person on their side if unresponsive.

redFlags.label: Possible stroke
redFlags.message: Sudden facial drooping, arm weakness or difficulty speaking is a stroke until proven otherwise. Treatment works only within a few hours.
redFlags.action: Call emergency services now and note the exact time symptoms began.

redFlags.label: Seizure
redFlags.message: A first seizure needs assessment to find the cause and to advise on driving and safety.
redFlags.action: Seek urgent assessment today. Call emergency services if the seizure lasted over five minutes or a second one followed.

redFlags.label: Significant gastrointestinal bleeding
redFlags.message: Vomiting blood, or passing black tarry stools, means bleeding inside the digestive tract.
redFlags.action: Go to an emergency department now.

redFlags.label: New jaundice
redFlags.message: Yellowing of the skin or eyes always needs blood tests to find out why.

redFlags.label: Sudden loss of vision
redFlags.message: Sight lost suddenly in one or both eyes needs assessment the same hour, whatever the cause.
redFlags.action: Go to an eye emergency department now.

redFlags.label: Thoughts of self-harm
redFlags.message: Thoughts of harming yourself or of being better off dead deserve help today. You do not have to be in crisis to reach out.
redFlags.action: Contact your doctor, a crisis line, or go to an emergency department now. If you are in immediate danger, call emergency services.

redFlags.label: New confusion coming on over hours or days
redFlags.message: Confusion that has come on over hours or days, or that comes and goes through the day, is delirium until proven otherwise. It is caused by something else -- an infection, a drug, pain, retention -- and that cause needs finding today.
redFlags.action: Seek same-day medical assessment. Take a list of all medications. Call emergency services if they are drowsy, feverish or cannot be roused properly.

disclaimer: This tool provides information about possible causes of symptoms. It is not a diagnosis and it cannot examine you. It does not replace assessment by a qualified clinician. If you feel very unwell, or your symptoms are getting rapidly worse, seek medical help immediately regardless of what this tool says.
